architecture_decisions.decision: Use Next.js full-stack monorepo plus separate TypeScript BullMQ worker; do not introduce a separate backend framework.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Simplifies MVP while preserving independent scaling for long-running Playwright/OCR/AI jobs.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use BullMQ/Redis for all long-running tasks, including scraping, OCR, AI enrichment, export generation, sync, retries, and re-enrichment jobs.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Accepted risks require retryable, resumable, observable background jobs.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use UniversalCatalogItem base table plus type-specific JSON attributes and normalized first-class fields.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Mitigates universal item schema risk without premature per-type table explosion.

architecture_decisions.decision: Preserve AI Capability Router plus Provider Adapter architecture as the stable interface for all AI integrations.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Business workflows call AI capabilities and never provider SDKs directly.

architecture_decisions.decision: All catalog writes go through deterministic validation from Discovery Session candidate to Catalog Item.
architecture_decisions.rationale: AI never writes directly to inventory/catalog.

architecture_decisions.decision: Tenant isolation is enforced at application query boundaries and database constraints using tenant_id/workspace_id on tenant-owned records.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Accepted security risk requires explicit tenant boundary.

architecture_decisions.decision: PostgreSQL full-text search is MVP search; external search is deferred.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Avoid unnecessary infrastructure until catalog size proves need.

architecture_decisions.decision: Centralize business logic in shared Domain Services using Route Handler -> Service -> Repository -> Prisma and Worker -> Service -> Repository -> Prisma flows.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Keeps route handlers, server actions, and worker processors thin while sharing business logic across web and worker.

architecture_decisions.decision: Organize implementation as a pnpm monorepo with apps/web, apps/worker, and shared packages: domain, ai, scrapers, shared, validation, types.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Supports shared types and domain logic across the web app and worker without duplicating business rules.

architecture_decisions.decision: Treat scraping and AI enrichment as independent pipelines; persist normalized source records so enrichment can be rerun without re-scraping.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Allows provider swaps, prompt/capability changes, validation improvements, and re-enrichment without repeating fragile scraping work.

risks_and_constraints.risk: Playwright jobs may be blocked or rate-limited by vendor anti-bot controls.
risks_and_constraints.mitigation: Bounded crawling, per-vendor throttles, manual fallback, failure states, and Stage 6 representative tests.

risks_and_constraints.risk: Tenant isolation bug could expose catalog data or AI credentials across workspaces.
risks_and_constraints.mitigation: Tenant_id on all tenant tables, service-level authorization guards, integration tests, credential encryption.

risks_and_constraints.risk: Universal Catalog Item JSON attributes become unqueryable if too much domain data is pushed into unstructured fields.
risks_and_constraints.mitigation: Keep common searchable fields normalized; reserve JSON attributes for type-specific optional fields.

risks_and_constraints.risk: Queue observability is insufficient for users to understand import state.
risks_and_constraints.mitigation: ImportJob and ImportJobEvent entities; user-visible statuses; Sentry/log metrics.

risks_and_constraints.risk: Cloud AI provider costs vary with extraction volume.
risks_and_constraints.mitigation: Per-workspace provider credentials, job cost logging, provider routing, local Ollama option.

frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui-compatible component primitives
frontend.state: Server Components and server actions for standard flows; client state only for interactive discovery/catalog workflows

backend.framework: Next.js route handlers and server actions
backend.api_style: Route Handler -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma for REST-style JSON endpoints and app-owned mutations
backend.background_jobs: Separate TypeScript BullMQ worker on Redis for all long-running tasks

packages.packages/domain: Domain services, use cases, orchestration, business logic, and service interfaces consumed by web and worker.
packages.packages/ai: AI Capability Router, provider adapter interfaces, provider implementations, request/response normalization, and provider health checks.
packages.packages/scrapers: Playwright website discovery, navigation tree extraction, PDF/OCR import connectors, and raw artifact collection.
packages.packages/shared: Shared utilities, config helpers, logging, errors, constants, and cross-cutting primitives.
packages.packages/validation: Deterministic validation rules, duplicate checks, SKU/price/category rules, and candidate-to-catalog import gates.
packages.packages/types: Shared TypeScript types, DTOs, schemas, queue payloads, and API contracts.

domain_service_layer.request_flow: Route Handler / Server Action -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.worker_flow: BullMQ Processor -> Domain Service -> Repository -> Prisma -> PostgreSQL
domain_service_layer.rule: Business logic lives in domain services and validation package, not directly inside route handlers, server actions, or queue processors.

database.search: PostgreSQL full-text search for MVP; external search deferred until scale evidence exists

storage.usage: PDF uploads, generated PDFs/PNGs, import snapshots, rendered DOM snapshots when retained

authentication.tenant_model: Workspace maps to Clerk organization and application workspace_id
authentication.authorization: Application-enforced RBAC with workspace_owner for MVP

hosting_and_deployment.workers: Fly.io TypeScript worker service with Playwright runtime
hosting_and_deployment.observability: Sentry plus structured logs and queue/job metrics

testing_stack.route_integration: Vitest against route handlers/server actions through domain services
testing_stack.worker_integration: Vitest against BullMQ processors through domain services
testing_stack.security: tenant-isolation integration tests and credential handling checks

ai_and_external_services.status: stable interface for all AI integrations

pipeline_architecture.scraping_pipeline: External source -> connector/scraper -> raw import artifact -> normalized source record -> Discovery Session candidate seed
pipeline_architecture.ai_enrichment_pipeline: Normalized source record or catalog candidate -> AI Capability Router -> Provider Adapter -> enrichment result -> validation -> candidate/catalog update
pipeline_architecture.separation_rule: Scraping collects and normalizes source data; AI enrichment is independently repeatable and can re-enrich stored normalized source records without re-scraping.
pipeline_architecture.re_enrichment_support: Persist normalized source records and import artifacts with version/source hashes so users can rerun enrichment after changing provider, prompt, capability route, or validation rules.

selected_stack.rationale: A Next.js full-stack monorepo with a separate BullMQ worker is the simplest scalable architecture: route handlers and server actions stay thin, all business logic is centralized in shared domain services, workers reuse the same domain services, scraping and AI enrichment remain independent pipelines, and the AI Capability Router/Provider Adapter interface remains stable for all AI integrations.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Too risky for Playwright/OCR/AI jobs; workers must scale and run independently.
Adds a second language while frontend, Playwright, and worker ecosystem remain TypeScript-heavy.
Over-engineered before scale evidence; monorepo packages plus separate worker are enough.
Unnecessary until catalog scale proves PostgreSQL full-text insufficient.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Approve the simplified scalable monorepo architecture: Next.js full-stack app, separate BullMQ worker for all long-running tasks, shared Domain Service layer, shared packages, AI Capability Router/Provider Adapter interface, and independent scraping/enrichment pipelines.

alternatives_considered.reason: Too risky for Playwright/OCR/AI jobs; workers must scale and run independently.
Adds a second language while frontend, Playwright, and worker ecosystem remain TypeScript-heavy.
Over-engineered before scale evidence; monorepo packages plus separate worker are enough.
Unnecessary until catalog scale proves PostgreSQL full-text insufficient.

downstream_impact: Stage 4 can design UX around asynchronous import jobs, Discovery Sessions, catalog review, and provider settings.
Stage 5 can create implementation slices around workspace/auth, vendors, import jobs, discovery sessions, catalog, AI adapters, and exports.
Stage 6 must include representative Playwright import tests, tenant-isolation tests, queue retry/resume tests, and validation gate tests.
revision_notes: User requested explicit constraints: no separate backend framework, BullMQ worker retained, shared domain service layer, monorepo packages, AI router/adapters preserved, and scraping/enrichment separated.

deployment_units.component: Next.js web app, route handlers, and server actions
TypeScript BullMQ worker with Playwright runtime

queue_model.retry_policy: bounded exponential backoff with max attempts per job type
queue_model.idempotency: job id + workspace id + source hash
queue_model.dead_letter: failed terminal state with user-visible recovery

storage_model.pdf_uploads: B2 object keys namespaced by workspace/vendor
storage_model.exports: B2 generated artifacts with signed download URLs

monorepo_deployment_model.apps/web: deployed to Vercel; consumes packages/domain, packages/ai, packages/shared, packages/validation, packages/types
monorepo_deployment_model.apps/worker: deployed to Fly.io; consumes packages/domain, packages/ai, packages/scrapers, packages/shared, packages/validation, packages/types
